explanation: Nitrogen gas (N2) comprises approximately 78% of the Earth's atmosphere, but plants cannot use gaseous nitrogen directly, making it a limiting factor. The nitrogen cycle converts N2 into usable forms: 1) Nitrogen fixation is carried out by certain cyanobacteria and bacteria, converting nitrogen gas into ammonium ions (NH4+), which plants can assimilate. 2) Nitrification produces nitrates (NO3-), another usable form. Gaseous nitrogen is converted to nitrates in the atmosphere by lightning, meteor trails, and cosmic radiation, while soil ammonium is converted to nitrate by nitrifying bacteria. Plants absorb ammonium and nitrates to synthesize proteins and amino acids. 3) Denitrification is the conversion of nitrate back into nitrogen gas by denitrifying bacteria, completing the cycle.

questions.q: What is nitrogen fixation and what organisms perform it?
opts: Conversion of nitrates to gaseous nitrogen by plants
Conversion of nitrogen gas to ammonium ions by some cyanobacteria and bacteria
Assimilation of nitrates into amino acids by herbivores
Conversion of soil ammonium to nitrate by terrestrial fungi
